Katanga Mining Ltd Unveils New Copper Refining Technology in DRC

Katanga Mining Ltd, a leading player in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s metals and mining sector, today announced the launch of its proprietary copper refining technology at its Kolwezi facility. The new process, developed over the past three years, is expected to boost production efficiency and enhance the purity of copper output.

Company executives say the technology, dubbed “Katanga PureFlow,” will allow the Kolwezi plant to refine copper to a 99.99% purity level, meeting increasing global demand for high-grade copper. The company estimates that the new process will increase annual output by 12% to approximately 270,000 metric tonnes.

“This launch marks a significant milestone for Katanga Mining Ltd and the Congolese mining industry,” said CEO Jean-Michel Kasongo at a press briefing in Lubumbashi. “Katanga PureFlow will not only increase our competitiveness but also support sustainable economic development in the region.”

The Democratic Republic of the Congo holds some of the world’s largest copper reserves, and the mining sector is a major contributor to national GDP. Industry analysts note that Katanga Mining Ltd’s investment in refining technology could help strengthen the DRC’s position as a key supplier in the global copper market.

Elise Mubenga, an analyst at Kinshasa-based consultancy Resource Insights, commented, “With demand for copper rising, especially in the energy and electronics sectors, innovations like PureFlow are vital for the DRC to capture more value from its resources.”

The company has also pledged to increase local hiring and expand its technical training program in partnership with the Lualaba Mining Institute. “We are committed to empowering Congolese talent and ensuring our operations benefit local communities,” said Kasongo.

Shares in Katanga Mining Ltd closed up 2.1% on the Kinshasa Stock Exchange after the announcement.
